facts.text: I wanted to love the toaster but it doesn’t toast evenly.
I bought a simple 4-slice toaster in 2009.
I expected this toaster to have a bagel feature but it doesn’t.
I found that the toaster cannot accommodate four slices.
When I make breakfast for the family, I toast two slices at a time.
Some spots on the toast are nearly burnt while others are barely toasted.
When I toast English muffins, setting 3 is too light and setting 4 is burnt.
Because the toaster is digital, there is no in-between setting.
I read the included book and put the slices in the center as it states for two slices, but I still got bad results.
I am going to donate this toaster and purchase a different brand.
I found that the toaster does not toast the bread near the top of the slice as much as the remainder of the slice.
I think the digital deal is neat but it leaves toasting on 2 and then toasting a bit more.
I found that a 3 setting makes toast dark and dry.
I prefer the dial type controller on older toasters because it lets me dial in the right amount of time.
I think the toaster looks nice and is easy to operate.
I have to baby sit my toast with this toaster.
I was taken aback by how large but lightweight/flimsy the toaster felt upon receiving it.
I recommend measuring the space before buying because the toaster gets super hot at least 12 inches above it under an angled roofline.
I need to pull the toaster forward so the ceiling doesn’t get over hot.
The sides of the toaster get really hot.
The toaster cord is not super long.
The cord length is 27 inches.
The cord comes out near-ish the plunger.
The toaster eject is jarring and loud.
The first time, my cat flew straight into the air and then ripped out of the room.
Over time, the eject seems a bit less jarring.
The first time I used it, I followed the recommendation to run it without bread to burn off the initial strong chemical smell.
I think the weight of bread may slow the eject down.
I would not necessarily recommend the toaster but I will keep it.
My next toaster will probably be the America’s Test Kitchen highly-rated $100 Breville.
This toaster cost $35 (or $40 minus a $5 coupon).
I like the ability to toast 2 long slices (artisanal sourdough) or 4 English muffins at a time.
I appreciate the wide slots for specialty bakery breads that wouldn’t fit in a normal toaster.
I appreciate the ability to cook four slices of standard bread at once.
I like the timing function for trying to get all parts of the meal ready at the same time.
I found the toaster doesn’t have a deep enough well and/or the toaster elements don’t come up high enough, so the top of the bread doesn’t get toasted.
I have to turn the bread over and toast it longer on that side.
When I do that, the middle of the bread gets too well done.
I like my toast fairly well done but I hate hard toast.
I want a one-and-done toasting situation.
I found the clean-out tray at the bottom never seems to have much on it when I empty it.
I found the toaster spews crumbs and seeds all over the counter even when the clean-up tray is inserted.
I’m glad I didn’t pay much for this toaster because the cons outweigh the pros.
I am going to look for a new toaster and read the reviews carefully and thoroughly this time.
I found the toaster only toasts about 3/4 of the bread.
I think the toaster needs calibration and the bread needs to go down more into the heating elements.
I found the toaster settings are 1=toast, 2=dark toast, 3=burnt toast, and 4&5=flames/fire.
I wish I could calibrate the settings.
I love the thin nature of the machine.
I like the length of the toaster for homemade breads.
I found that when bread is in the toaster, the top of the bread sticks out and doesn’t toast.
I found that the bottom of the bread is too dark.
I sent the toaster back.
I found the toaster consistently toasts the bottom part of the bread or bagel more darkly than the top part.
I found that evenness has not been a strong point for this toaster.
I found that the toaster cooks hot out of the box.
My first two attempts for “level 4” Golden haven’t worked.
I will try a 2 setting and work our way up.
I found the toaster makes a loud clank when toast pops up.
I found that the toaster leaves all toast partially untoasted.
I found that the toaster has a physical lever to push the toast down.
I found that I can’t push the lever up to end the toast cycle early.
I have to push a touch button on the side to cancel the toast cycle.
I think the cancel function is controlled by a computer chip along with the toast level and will probably fail years before the rest of the hardware.
I found that the toasting rack doesn’t descend fully into the toasting zone.
I found that even a bagel doesn’t toast all the way at the top.
I found that the bottom gets overly brown.
I usually stand by the toaster and rotate the pieces.
I think rotating pieces defeats the purpose of the toaster.

keyphrases: toasting two slices at a time
